about: The second part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities: days eight to eleven. It opens by joining this book to its companion, the Liberation through Wearing: to proclaim the two together is like setting turquoise on gold. Then the dead person is told that, because he did not recognise the peaceful bardo, he has had to wander on, and that the blood-drinking wrathful deities now dawn. On the eighth day comes Buddha Heruka, dark maroon, with three heads, six arms and four legs spread wide, blazing, laughing and roaring, his hands holding a wheel, an axe, a sword, a bell, a plough and an implement the scan does not show, embraced by his consort Buddhakrodhīśvarī; he dawns from the east of the dead person's own brain. He is not to be feared: he is the dead person's own yidam, and in truth Vairocana with his consort, and to recognise him is to be freed. Those who flee in terror meet, on the ninth day, Vajra Heruka, who is Vajrasattva; on the tenth, Ratna Heruka, who is Ratnasambhava; on the eleventh, after those whose bad habits make them see the deities as Lords of Death, Padma Heruka, who is Amitābha. Each has his colour, his six implements and his consort, and dawns from his own quarter of the brain; each time the same words are spoken: do not fear, recognise him as the form of your own awareness, and recognising and freedom come at once.

sentences.w: འདི་ དང་ བཏགས་གྲོལ་ གཉིས་ བསྒྲགས་པས༔ གསེར་ གྱི་ མཎྜལ་ ལ་ གཡུའི་ ཕྲ་ བཀོད་པ་ དང་ འདྲ་བས་ བསྒྲགས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: This and Wearing-Liberation, two, proclaimed-by: gold's maṇḍala on turquoise's inlay arranged with alike-because, proclaiming do!
sentences.i: To proclaim the two together, this and the Liberation through Wearing, is like setting turquoise inlay on a golden maṇḍala: so proclaim them.
sentences.n: The part begins on the line where the last ended, after the praise of the Great Liberation through Hearing. 'di, 'this', is that book. Btags grol, 'Liberation through Wearing' (btags, the past stem of 'dogs, 'to tie on, attach'; grol, 'freed'), is the name of a companion text of the same cycle, mantras that free by being worn on the body; it is translated in the idiomatic line. gnyis, 'the two'. bsgrags pas, 'by proclaiming': bsgrags is the past stem of sgrog, 'to proclaim, to cry aloud' (sgrog / bsgrags / bsgrag / sgrogs). gser gyi maN+Dal, 'a golden maṇḍala', here the round plate of an offering, which is set with precious things; g.yu'i phra, 'inlay of turquoise' (phra, 'fine work, inlay'), is doubtful on the image ([?]): one stack with a pha-like body and a subscript r, where the other recension has 'phra. bkod pa, 'set, arranged'; dang 'dra bas, 'because it is like'. bsgrags par gyis shig, 'do the proclaiming!': gyis shig is the command 'do!', as in the parts before. The print runs dang and btags together across the line join (the nga ends against the frame), here divided.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ ཐོས་གྲོལ་ གྱི་ དགོས་པ་ བསྟན་ ནས༔ ད་ ནི་ ཁྲོ་བོའི་ བར་དོ་ འཆར་ཚུལ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པར་ བྱ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Thus Hearing-Liberation's purpose shown, then: now, as-for, wrathful-ones' between, dawning-manner face-introducing is-to-be-done, and:
sentences.i: Now that the purpose of the Liberation through Hearing has been shown, the way the bardo of the wrathful deities dawns is to be pointed out.
sentences.n: dgos pa, 'need, purpose', what the reading is for; the other recension has dgos ched, with the same sense. bstan nas, 'having shown' (bstan, the past stem of ston). khro bo'i is doubtful on the image ([?]) though the words are those of the title of text ga (009). ngo sprad par bya, 'is to be pointed out', with bya, the future of byed, as in bstan par bya in 009; the other recension has the present ngo sprod. The print runs dgos and pa together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ ལན་ གསུམ་ བོས་ ནས་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the dead-one's by-name three times called, then, these-words: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Call the dead person by name three times and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: The formula of the peaceful days (004–007), here with lan gsum, 'three times' (lan, 'time, turn'), and bos nas, 'having called' (bos, the past stem of 'bod, 'to call'), where the other recension has bos la (and de yang for yang). kyai is written with the doubled vowel sign, as in the pilot; the next calls in this part have kye.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ གོང་དུ་ ཞི་བའི་ བར་དོ་ ཤར་ ཡང་ ངོས་ མ་ ཟིན་པས་ ད་དུང་ འདིར་ འཁྱམས་པ་ དགོས་ བྱུང་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Your before-at peaceful's between dawned though, recognition not seized-because, still here wandering must came-about is.
sentences.i: The peaceful bardo dawned before you, but you did not recognise it, and so you have had to wander here still.
sentences.n: khyod kyi gong du, 'before you, earlier for you'; the other recension has khyod kyis, 'by you', which goes with ngos ma zin, 'you did not recognise'. shar yang, 'though it dawned' (shar, the past of 'char). ngos ma zin pas, 'because the face was not seized': ma, the 'not' of the past. da dung, 'still, yet'. 'khyams pa dgos byung ba yin no, 'it has come about that you must wander': dgos, 'must, need'; byung, the past of 'byung, 'to happen'. dgos and byung are both marked doubtful ([?]) and are not in the other recension, which has only 'khyams pa yin no, 'you are wandering'; the reader saw them fairly clearly at twelve times enlargement, but a second reader has not confirmed them.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ ཞག་ བརྒྱད་པ་ ལ༔ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ཁྲོ་བོའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ངོས་ ཟིན་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Now, as-for, day eighth on: blood-drinking wrathful-ones' deity-host dawning comes. Not distracted-way recognition seizing do!
sentences.i: Now on the eighth day the host of blood-drinking wrathful deities will dawn. Do not be distracted: recognise them.
sentences.n: zhag brgyad pa, 'the eighth day' (brgyad, 'eight', with -pa, which makes the ordinal), counting on from the seven days of the peaceful deities. khrag 'thung, 'blood-drinker' (Sanskrit heruka), as in 009. 'char du 'ong ngo, 'will come to dawn'. ngos zin par gyis shig, 'do the seizing of the face', recognise, as on the first day (003).

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ དཔལ་ཆེན་ བུདྡྷ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ སྨུག་ནག་ དབུ་ གསུམ་ ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ ཞབས་ བཞི་ བསྒྲད་པ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Great-Glorious Buddha-Heruka so-called, body-colour dark-maroon, heads three, hands six, feet four spread-wide(?),
sentences.i: O child of noble family, the great and glorious Buddha Heruka, dark maroon in colour, with three heads, six arms and four legs spread wide,
sentences.n: The first of the five blood-drinkers, one for each buddha family; the description runs as a string of phrases, each closed by ༔ and most by -pa, 'being, having', down to the verb at the end of the sentence. dpal chen, 'great glorious' (dpal, 'glory'; chen, 'great'), a title of the herukas. Buddha he ru ka, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, 'the heruka of the buddha family'; buddha is crushed against the frame at the line end and doubtful ([?]), though the other recension has the same name. zhes bya ba, 'so called'. smug nag, 'dark maroon' (smug, 'purplish brown'; nag, 'black'). dbu, 'head', phyag, 'hand, arm', and zhabs, 'foot, leg', are the respectful words. bsgrad[?] pa: the stack is taller than ga with ra and seems to carry an s on top; the other recension has bgrad pa, which the print itself has for the three herukas after this one; bgrad pa is 'spread wide, set apart', of legs planted in a wide stance, and the sense is the same either way. The print runs buddha and he together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཞལ་ གཡས་ དཀར་བ༔ གཡོན་ དམར་བ༔ དབུས་ སྨུག་ནག་ཏུ་ ཡོད་པ༔ སྐུ་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཕུང་པོ་ འབར་བ༔ སྤྱན་ དགུ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ སྡང་མིག་ཏུ་ གཟིགས་པ༔ སྨིན་མ་ གློག་ བཞིན་དུ་ འཁྱུག་པ༔ མཆེ་བ་ ཟངས་ཡག་ཏུ་ འབར་བ༔
sentences.l: Face right white, left red, centre dark-maroon-as being; body light's mass blazing; eyes nine fearsome's glare-as gazing; brows lightning like flashing; fangs copper-fine(?)-ly blazing;
sentences.i: his right face white, his left red, his centre one dark maroon; his body a blazing mass of light; his nine eyes staring in a terrible glare; his brows flashing like lightning; his fangs gleaming like copper(?);
sentences.n: zhal g.yas, 'the right face': the other recension has g.yas zhal and g.yon zhal; the print names the face once. smug nag tu yod pa, 'is (in) dark maroon', with -tu. sku 'od kyi phung po 'bar ba, 'the body blazing as a mass of light'. spyan, 'eye', and gzigs, 'to look', are respectful words: three eyes in each of the three faces. sdang mig, 'hostile eye, glare' (sdang, 'hatred'). smin ma, 'eyebrow'; 'khyug, 'to flash'. mche ba, 'fang, tusk'. zangs yag tu is not sure: zangs is 'copper' and yag 'good, fine'; it is taken as 'with a copper gleam', and the other recension has the same words. smug[?] at the line end is doubtful on the image. The print runs smug and nag, and zangs and yag, together across the line joins; both are divided here.

sentences.w: ཨ་ལ་ལ་ དང་ ཧ་ཧའི་ གད་རྒྱང་ སྒྲོག་པ༔ ཤའུ་ ཞེས་པ་ དང་ བཤུགས་ ཀྱི་ སྒྲ་ ཆེན་པོ་ སྒྲོག་པ༔ དབུ་སྐྲ་ དམར་སེར་ གྱེན་དུ་ འཕྱོ་ ཞིང་ འབར་བ༔ ཉི་ཟླ་ དང༔ སྦྲུལ་ ནག་ དང༔ ཐོད་སྐམ་ ཀྱི་ དབུར་ བརྒྱན་པ༔
sentences.l: A-la-la and ha-ha's(?) loud-laughter sounding; sha'u(?) so-called and whistling's sound great sounding; head-hair red-yellow upward(?) streaming and blazing; sun-moon and, snake black and, skull-dry with(?) head-on adorned;
sentences.i: crying 'a la la!' and laughing aloud, 'ha ha!'; sounding the cry 'sha'u!' and a great whistling; his red-gold hair streaming upward and blazing; his head adorned with the sun and moon, black snakes and dry skulls;
sentences.n: a la la, a cry of joy or wonder; ha ha, the sound of laughter, here with -'i, 'of': ha ha'i is doubtful ([?]), for the reader sees no e-vowel where the other recension has ha he'i. gad rgyang, 'a far-carrying laugh' (gad, 'laugh'; rgyang, 'far'). sgrog pa, 'crying out, sounding', the present stem of the verb whose past is bsgrags in the first sentence. sha'u, a cry, is doubtful ([?]); the traces fit the other recension's sha'u. zhes pa, 'so called', 'the (sound) called'. bshugs is taken as 'whistling, hissing'; the other recension has bshug pa'i; the sense is not sure. dbu skra, 'hair of the head' (respectful); dmar ser, 'red-yellow', orange or tawny. gyen du, 'upward': du is doubtful ([?]), and the print runs it and 'phyo together across the line join, here divided. 'phyo, 'to stream, to fly in the wind'. dbur, 'on the head' (dbu with -r). thod skam, 'dry skull' (thod, 'skull'; skam, 'dry'); kyi, 'of', where kyis, 'by, with', is meant (the other recension has gyis); the print is kept and read so. The other recension has here two phrases: the sun, moon and dry skulls adorn the head, and the black snakes and fresh skulls (thod rlon) the body; the print puts all three on the head and has no fresh skulls.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ གཡས་ ཀྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ འཁོར་ལོ༔ བར་པ་ ན་ དགྲ་སྟ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ རལ་གྲི༔ གཡོན་ གྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ དྲིལ་བུ༔ བར་བ་ ན་ ཐོང་གཤོལ༔ ཐ་མ་ བསྣམས་པར༔
sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in wheel; middle in axe; last in sword; left's first in bell; middle in plough; last [ … ] holding,
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a wheel, the middle an axe, the last a sword; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a plough, and the last [an implement the scan does not show];
sentences.n: dang po na, 'in the first'; bar pa, 'the middle one'; tha ma, 'the last': the six hands are counted on each side from the top. 'khor lo, 'wheel'; dgra sta, 'axe' (dgra, 'enemy'; sta, 'axe'); ral gri, 'sword'; dril bu, 'bell'; thong gshol, 'plough'. bar ba is the print's spelling of bar pa. Two places on this line cannot be filled. (1) After bar ba na the print has an uninked blank about the width of a word, where the other recension has bhan dha, 'skull-cup', in the middle left hand. A word was probably erased from the block or never cut: nothing is printed, so nothing is written. (2) After tha ma two stacks stand where the name of the implement in the last left hand should be, and they cannot be read in the scan, even enlarged ten times: the first is a ka- or kha-like letter with something below it, the second has a head like Ta over a curled subscript. They are left out of the text, which reads tha ma bsnams par. A khaṭvāṅga (khaTwaM, the staff topped with skulls) is possible, but it is not confirmed, and the other recension gives no candidate, for its item for the last hand, thong gshol, already stands in the print in the middle hand. bsnams par, 'holding', the respectful word: with -r it runs on to the next phrases.
sentences.gap: p. 92 l. 1: Buddha Heruka's last left-hand implement (two stacks unreadable in the scan)

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ བུདྡྷ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་ མགུལ་ ནས་ འཁྱུད་ ཅིང༔ གཡོན་པས་ དུང་ དམར་ ཞལ་དུ་ སྟོབ་པ༔
sentences.l: The mother Buddhakrodhīśvarī body to embracing; right-by neck at embracing and; left-by conch red mouth-to feeding;
sentences.i: his consort Buddhakrodhīśvarī embraces his body: with her right hand she holds him round the neck, and with her left she puts a red conch to his mouth;
sentences.n: Buddha kro ti shwa ri ma, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters with the Tibetan feminine -ma: Buddhakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the buddha family' (krodha, 'wrath'; īśvarī, 'lady'); kro ti is the print's spelling of krodhī, and the other recension writes bhuddha. sku la 'khril ba, 'winding about his body', as of the consorts in 007 and 008. g.yas pas, g.yon pas, 'with the right, with the left' (g.yas pa, 'the right one', with -s, 'by'). mgul, 'neck', the respectful word; mgul nas 'khyud, 'embraces at the neck'; the other recension has yab kyi mgul nas, 'the father's neck', and 'khyud pa. dung dmar, 'a red conch', a conch shell; what makes it red is not said. zhal du stob pa, 'giving to his mouth, feeding' (zhal, 'mouth, face', respectful).

sentences.w: རྐན་སྒྲ་ ཐུག་ཆོམ་ དང་ འུར་སྒྲ་ འབྲུག་ ལྡིར་བ་ ཙམ་པ༔ རྡོ་རྗེ་ འབར་བའི་ སྤུ་སེབ་ ནས་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ མེ་ འབར་བ༔ ཁྱུང་ གིས་ བཏེགས་པའི་ གདན་ ལ་ བརྐྱང་བསྐུམ་དུ་ བཞུགས་པར༔ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ཤར་ ནས་ རང་ གི་ མངོན་སུམ་ ཉི་ དེ་ཀ་ ལྟར་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Palate-sound clacking(?) and roaring-sound thunder booming as-much-as being; vajra blazing's hair-gaps from wisdom's fire blazing; garuḍa by(?) lifted's seat on stretched-drawn-in-ly seated-as: own's brain's east from own's directly(?) just-that like dawns.
sentences.i: with a clacking of the tongue and a roar as loud as thunder; the fire of wisdom blazing from between his hairs, which blaze like vajras; sitting with one leg stretched out and one drawn in on a seat borne up by a garuḍa: so he dawns from the east of your own brain, before your very eyes.
sentences.n: rkan sgra, 'the sound of the palate', a clicking or clacking made with the tongue; thug chom is taken as a word for that sound; the sense is not sure. 'ur sgra, 'a din, a roar' (008). 'brug ldir ba tsam pa, 'as much as the booming of thunder' (008): the print has no verb after it; the other recension has tsam sgrog pa, 'sounding as loud as', and the print's tsam pa, 'being as much as', is kept and read so. rdo rje 'bar ba'i spu seb nas, 'from between the hairs blazing (like) vajras': spu, 'hair of the body'; seb is the print's spelling of gseb, 'gap, midst', which the other recension has; rdo rje 'bar ba'i may also be read 'of the blazing vajra', the body. ye shes kyi me, 'the fire of wisdom'. khyung, 'garuḍa', the great bird; gis, 'by', is doubtful ([?]): a narrow trace stands between gi and the next letter. btegs pa'i, 'lifted', the past stem of 'degs, 'to lift', where the other recension has the present 'degs. brkyang bskum du, 'stretched and drawn in', one leg out and one bent; bzhugs par, 'sitting', the respectful word, with -r running on to the verb. klad pa, 'brain'; shar, here 'east', as lho, 'south', and nub, 'west', in the days after. The other recension has klad pa'i nang nas thon nas, 'emerging from within the brain', the place of the centre, where Buddha Heruka belongs; the print has 'east', which it also has for Vajra Heruka on the ninth day, and is followed. rang gi mngon sum, 'in your own direct sight' (mngon sum, 'manifest, directly perceived'); the other recension has rang la, 'to you'. nyi[?] de ka ltar, 'just so': nyi is doubtful and may stand for nyid, 'itself, very', with its final d not printed; the other recension has mngon sum de ka ltar without it, and it is translated as if absent. 'char ro, 'dawns', with the sentence-ending -o after -r. The print runs gi and mngon together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ སྐུར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Him at not fear! Not be-afraid! Not be-terrified! Own's knowing's body-as face-knowing do!
sentences.i: Do not fear him. Do not be afraid. Do not be terrified. Recognise him as the form of your own awareness.
sentences.n: The three commands of the first day (003), ma 'jigs shig, ma skrag cig, ma dngangs shig, with ma, 'not', before the verb and shig (cig after -g) for the command; dngangs is the print's spelling, as in the parts before. rig pa'i skur, 'as the body of awareness' (sku with -r, 'as'): the deity is to be known as the form one's own awareness takes. The other recension has rang rig pa'i, 'self-aware', without gi.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ དོན་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དངོས་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ དང་ གྲོལ་བ་ དུས་མཉམ་མོ༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid! Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Vairocana father-mother itself is-because, not fear! Face-knowing and freeing time-same.
sentences.i: He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid. In truth he is the Blessed One Vairocana himself with his consort, so do not fear. To recognise him and to be freed are one and the same moment.
sentences.n: yi dam, the deity one takes as one's own in practice (009). don la, 'in meaning, in truth' (don, 'meaning, point', with la). Each blood-drinker is one of the five buddhas of the peaceful days in wrathful form: Buddha Heruka is Vairocana, the buddha of the first day. dngos, 'actual, itself'. ma 'jigs shig, 'do not fear!', where the other recension has ma skrag cig. dus mnyam mo, 'are of the same time' (dus, 'time'; mnyam, 'equal'), with the sentence-ending -o after -m; the other recension has dus mnyam du 'ong ngo, 'come at the same time', as the print has on the next three days.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ བསྒྲགས་པས༔ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment.
sentences.n: zhes, 'so', closes the words spoken to the dead person, from kye rigs kyi bu to here. bsgrags pas, 'because it is proclaimed' (bsgrags, as in the first sentence); the print closes it with ༔, which the other recension does not have. yi dam du, 'as the yidam'. gnyis su med par thim, 'dissolves without being two', as in 007 and 009. longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skur, 'as the body of perfect enjoyment', as in 004; the print has it only here of the four days.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ ལ་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་པས་ ངོ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ ན༔ ཞག་ དགུ་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ རྡོ་རྗེ་ རིགས་ ཀྱིས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: Again, him at terror-fright arisen, then, fled-because, face not meeting if: day ninth on blood-drinking vajra family by welcoming-for comes-because:
sentences.i: But if terror and fright arise at him and the dead person flees and does not recognise, on the ninth day the blood-drinkers of the vajra family come to meet him. So
sentences.n: dngangs skrag skyes nas, 'terror and fright having arisen' (skyes, the past of skye, 'to arise, be born'); bros pas, 'because he fled' (bros, the past of 'bros, 'to flee'); the other recension has skyes shing bros nas. ngo ma 'phrod na, 'if the face does not meet', if he does not recognise: ma ... na, 'if not'. zhag dgu pa, 'the ninth day' (dgu, 'nine'). rdo rje rigs, 'the vajra family', the family of Vajrasattva on the second day; kyis, 'by', marks who comes. bsu ba la 'ong, 'come to welcome', as in 004. 'ong bas, 'because they come', runs on to the next sentence. The print runs pa and la together across the line join, here divided; the other recension has yang zhag dgu pa la༔.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family!
sentences.i: Point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family,
sentences.n: The formula of the peaceful days, with bos, the past stem of 'bod, as in 006 and 007. Here the print has no ma yengs par nyon cig, 'listen without distraction', and no zhag dgu ba la, 'on the ninth day', both of which the other recension has before the name; the eighth and tenth days have the command.

sentences.w: ཁྲག་འཐུང་ རྡོ་རྗེ་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ བཛྲ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ མཐིང་ནག་ ཞལ་ གསུམ་ ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ ཞབས་ བཞི་ བགྲད་པ༔ ཞལ་ གཡས་ དཀར་བ༔ གཡོན་ དམར་བ༔ དབུས་ མཐིང་བ༔
sentences.l: Blood-drinking vajra family's Blessed-One Vajra-Heruka so-called, body-colour dark-blue, faces three, hands six, feet four spread-wide; face right white, left red, centre blue;
sentences.i: the blood-drinking Blessed One of the vajra family, called Vajra Heruka, dark blue in colour, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, his right face white, his left red, his centre one blue,
sentences.n: The eighth day's description, shorter. rdo rje rigs kyi, 'of the vajra family', where the other recension has kyis, 'by'. Badzra he ru ka, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, Vajra Heruka, 'the heruka of the vajra family'. mthing nag, 'dark blue' (mthing, 'blue'; nag, 'black'); mthing ba, 'blue'. zhal gsum, 'three faces', where the eighth day had dbu gsum, 'three heads'. bgrad pa, 'spread wide', as the other recension has on every day. zhal g.yas, 'the right face', where the other recension has g.yas alone.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ གཡས་ ཀྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ རྡོ་རྗེ༔ བར་བ་ ན་ བྷན་དྷ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ དགྲ་སྟ༔ གཡོན་ གྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ དྲིལ་བུ༔ བར་མ་ ན་ བྷན་དྷ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ མཐོང་ཤོལ༔
sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in vajra; middle in skull-cup; last in axe; left's first in bell; middle in skull-cup; last in plough(?);
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a vajra, the middle a skull-cup, the last an axe; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a skull-cup, the last a plough;
sentences.n: rdo rje, 'vajra', the thunderbolt sceptre. bhan dha, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters (bhāṇḍa, 'vessel'), the cup made from the top of a skull; there is one in each middle hand. bar ba and bar ma are both the print's spellings of bar pa, 'the middle one'; the other recension has bar ba in both places. mthong shol[?] is the print's spelling of thong gshol, 'plough', which the eighth day has and the other recension has here: a ma is added at the front, and the ga before sha is missing. The letter after mthong carries a naro and could be sha or zha, so the reading is doubtful; the sense is clear.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ བཛྲ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ ཡབ་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་ མགུལ་ ནས་ འཁྱུད་ ཅིང་༔ གཡོན་པས་ དུང་ དམར་ ཞལ་དུ་ སྟོབ་པ༔
sentences.l: The mother Vajrakrodhīśvarī father's body to embracing; right-by neck at embracing and; left-by conch red mouth-to feeding;
sentences.i: his consort Vajrakrodhīśvarī embraces the father's body: with her right hand she holds him round the neck, and with her left she puts a red conch to his mouth;
sentences.n: Vajrakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the vajra family'. yab kyi sku la, 'to the father's body'; the eighth day had sku la alone. The print has a tsheg before the ༔ after cing (ཅིང་༔), as also on the tenth day, where on the eighth and eleventh it has none.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ཤར་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Own's brain's east from emerged, then, oneself to dawning comes. Him at not fear! Not be-afraid! Not be-terrified!
sentences.i: He comes out of the east of your own brain and dawns before you. Do not fear him. Do not be afraid. Do not be terrified.
sentences.n: thon nas, 'having come out' (thon, 'to emerge'); the other recension has klad pa'i nang gi shar nas, 'from the east within the brain'. The east is the quarter of the vajra family. The print writes 'ong ngo contracted, as one stack: 'a with naro and a nga set beneath it (འྔོ); it is written out here as 'ong ngo, which the other recension has and which closes the same phrase elsewhere on these pages. It could also be read 'ong alone; the sense is the same.

sentences.w: དོན་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དངོས་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ དང་ གྲོལ་བ་ དུས་མཉམ་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Vajrasattva father-mother itself is-because, not be-afraid! Devotion do! Face-knowing and freeing time-same-at comes.
sentences.i: In truth he is the Blessed One Vajrasattva himself with his consort, so do not be afraid. Have devotion. Recognising and freedom come at one and the same time.
sentences.n: Vajra Heruka is Vajrasattva, the buddha of the second day (004). mos pa gyis shig, 'make devotion!' (mos pa, 'devotion, trust'), as on the peaceful days; the other recension has mos gus, 'devotion and respect', and no ma skrag cig before it. Here the print leaves out a whole passage that the other recension has, and that the print itself has on the eighth, tenth and eleventh days: 'recognise him as the form of your own awareness; he is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid'. dus mnyam du 'ong ngo, 'come at the same time'.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ བསྒྲགས་པས་ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས༔ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: As on the eighth day, but the print has no longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skur, 'in the body of perfect enjoyment', which the other recension has here; it has a ༔ after ngo shes nas.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ལས་སྒྲིབ་ ཆེ་བ་ རྣམས་ དེ་ ལ་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་པས་ ངོ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ ན༔ ཡང་ ཞག་ བཅུ་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་ རིགས་ ཀྱིས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: Again, karmic-obscuration great (plural) him at terror-fright arisen, then, fled-because, face not meeting if: again, day tenth on blood-drinking jewel's family by welcoming-for comes-because:
sentences.i: But those whose karmic obscurations are great feel terror and fright at him, flee and do not recognise. For them, on the tenth day, the blood-drinkers of the jewel family come to meet them. So
sentences.n: las sgrib, 'karmic obscuration' (las, 'deed, karma'; sgrib, 'obscuration'), the veil laid on the mind by one's past deeds; las sgrib che ba rnams, 'those (in whom) karmic obscuration is great', with rnams, the plural. zhag bcu pa, 'the tenth day' (bcu, 'ten'). rin po che'i rigs, 'the family of the jewel' (rin po che, 'precious thing, jewel'), the family of Ratnasambhava on the third day; the other recension has rin chen rigs and 'ong pas. The print has yang, 'again', before zhag, which the other recension does not have.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: As on the ninth day, here with ma yengs par nyon cig, as the other recension has.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བཅུ་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་ རིགས་ རཏྣ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ སེར་ནག་ ཞལ་ གསུམ་ ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ ཞབས་ བཞི་ བགྲད་པ༔ ཞལ་ གཡས་ དཀར་བ༔ གཡོན་ དམར་ དབུས་ སེར་ནག་ རབ་ འབར་བ༔
sentences.l: Day tenth on, blood-drinking jewel's family Ratna-Heruka so-called, body-colour dark-yellow, faces three, hands six, feet four spread-wide; face right white, left red, centre dark-yellow intensely(?) blazing;
sentences.i: On the tenth day the blood-drinker of the jewel family, called Ratna Heruka, dark yellow in colour, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, his right face white, his left red, his centre one dark yellow and blazing fiercely,
sentences.n: Ratna he ru ka, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, Ratna Heruka, 'the heruka of the jewel family' (ratna, 'jewel'). The print has rigs ratna he ru ka, 'the family, Ratna Heruka', where the other recension has rin chen rigs kyi༔ bcom ldan 'das ratna he ru ka, 'the Blessed One of the jewel family'; the print has neither kyi nor bcom ldan 'das, and rigs is read as standing for rigs kyi. ser nag, 'dark yellow'. g.yon dmar, 'the left red', without the -ba of the other days and of the other recension (g.yon dmar ba). rab[?] 'bar ba, 'blazing intensely' (rab, 'very, supremely'): after nag the reader sees more letters than nag 'bar ba needs and reads them rab, but two box-shaped letters in it cannot be told apart for certain (ba or 'a), so the reading is doubtful; the other recension has nag 'bar ba, without rab.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ གཡས་ ཀྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ རིན་པོ་ཆེ༔ བར་བ་ ན་ ཁཊྭཾ་ག༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ བེ་ཅོན་ བསྣམས་པ༔ གཡོན་ གྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ དྲིལ་བུ༔ བར་མ་ ན་ བྷན་དྷ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ ཏྲི་ཤུལ་ བསྣམས་པ༔
sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in jewel; middle in khaṭvāṅga; last in club holding; left's first in bell; middle in skull-cup; last in trident holding;
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a jewel, the middle a khaṭvāṅga, the last a club; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a skull-cup, the last a trident;
sentences.n: rin po che, 'jewel'. khaTwaM ga, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, khaṭvāṅga, the staff topped with skulls; the print writes it here in two syllables (ཁཊྭཾ་ག), and on the eleventh day as kha TwaM ga (ཁ་ཊྭཾ་ག); the other recension has kha TwaM ka. be con, 'club, cudgel'. tri shul, Sanskrit triśūla, 'trident', in a Tibetan spelling; the other recension has dri shul. bsnams pa, 'holding', closes each side. The print has bar ba on the right and bar ma on the left, where the other recension has bar ma and bar ba.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ རཏྣ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ ཡབ་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་ མགུལ་ ནས་ འཁྱུད་ ཅིང་༔ གཡོན་པས་ དུང་ དམར་ ཞལ་དུ་ སྟོབ་པ༔
sentences.l: The mother Ratnakrodhīśvarī father's body to embracing; right-by neck at embracing and; left-by conch red mouth-to feeding;
sentences.i: his consort Ratnakrodhīśvarī embraces the father's body: with her right hand she holds him round the neck, and with her left she puts a red conch to his mouth;
sentences.n: Ratnakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the jewel family'. The words are those of the ninth day, with the tsheg before ༔ after cing again. The print runs yab and kyi together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ལྷོ་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ སྐུར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Own's brain's south from emerged, then, oneself to dawning comes-because: him at not fear! Not be-afraid! Not be-terrified! Own's knowing's body-as face-knowing do!
sentences.i: He comes out of the south of your own brain and dawns before you. Do not fear him. Do not be afraid. Do not be terrified. Recognise him as the form of your own awareness.
sentences.n: lho nas, 'from the south', the quarter of the jewel family. 'ong bas, 'because he comes', runs on to the commands without ༔; the other recension has 'ong bas༔ and klad pa'i nang gi lho nas thon, 'emerging from the south within the brain'.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ དོན་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དངོས་ ཡིན་པས་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ དང་ གྲོལ་བ་ དུས་མཉམ་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid! Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava father-mother itself is-because, devotion do! Face-knowing and freeing time-same-at comes.
sentences.i: He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid. In truth he is the Blessed One Ratnasambhava himself with his consort, so have devotion. Recognising and freedom come at one and the same time.
sentences.n: Ratna Heruka is Ratnasambhava (Rin chen 'byung ldan, 'Source of Jewels'), the buddha of the third day (004). The print runs gyi and lha together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ བསྒྲགས་པས་ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: As on the ninth day; the other recension has ces for zhes, and it too names no body here.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ བག་ཆགས་ ངན་པའི་ དབང་ གིས་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ ཕྱིར་ བྲོས་པས༔ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ མ་ ཤེས་པར་ གཤིན་རྗེར་ མཐོང་ ནས་ ངོ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ ན༔
sentences.l: Again, thus face-introduced though, habitual-tendencies bad's power by terror-fright arisen, then, back fled-because: yidam-as not knowing-ly Death-Lords-as seen, then, face not meeting if:
sentences.i: But even when pointed out in this way, some, by the power of bad habitual tendencies, are struck with terror and fright and flee back; not knowing them as their yidam, they see them as Lords of Death and do not recognise.
sentences.n: ngo sprad kyang, 'though pointed out'. bag chags ngan pa'i dbang gis, 'by the power of bad habitual tendencies'; the other recension has bag chags ngan pas phyir 'khrid de, 'is drawn back by bad habitual tendencies', and here the print has phyir bros, 'flees back, flees away' (phyir, 'back, outward'). gshin rje, 'Lord of the Dead', Yama, and the fierce figures of his court; -r, 'as': gshin rjer mthong, 'sees as Lords of Death'. ngo ma 'phrod na, 'if he does not recognise', where the other recension has 'phrod pas, 'because he does not'. The print runs ngan and pa'i together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ཞག་ བཅུ་གཅིག་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ པདྨ་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ བསུ་བར་ འོང་བས༔ ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔
sentences.l: Again, day eleventh on blood-drinking lotus family's deity-host welcoming-for comes-because: again, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family!
sentences.i: On the eleventh day the host of blood-drinking deities of the lotus family comes to meet him. Point him out again: call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family,
sentences.n: zhag bcu gcig pa, 'the eleventh day' (bcu gcig, 'ten-one', eleven). padma rigs, 'the lotus family', the family of Amitābha on the fourth day. lha tshogs bsu bar 'ong, 'the deity host comes to meet'; the other recension has padma rigs kyis bsu ba la 'ong ste, 'the lotus family comes to meet'. As on the ninth day, the print has no 'listen without distraction' after kye rigs kyi bu, where the other recension has it. The print runs khrag and 'thung together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བཅུ་གཅིག་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ པདྨ་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ པདྨ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ སྐུ་མདོག་ དམར་ནག་ ཞལ་ གསུམ་ ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ ཞབས་ བཞི་ བགྲད་པ༔ ཞལ་ གཡས་ དཀར་བ། གཡོན་ སྔོན༔ དབུས་ དམར་ནག་ཏུ་ འབར་བ༔
sentences.l: Day eleventh on, blood-drinking lotus family's Blessed-One Padma-Heruka so-called, body-colour dark-red, faces three, hands six, feet four spread-wide; face right white, left blue; centre dark-red-as blazing;
sentences.i: On the eleventh day the blood-drinking Blessed One of the lotus family, called Padma Heruka, dark red in colour, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, his right face white, his left blue, his centre one blazing dark red,
sentences.n: Padma he ru ka, Padma Heruka, 'the heruka of the lotus family'. zhes bya ba runs on to sku mdog with no ༔ between them. dmar nag, 'dark red'. sngon, 'blue' (as in sngon po), where the other days have a red left face. The print closes dkar ba with the plain stroke ། instead of ༔, as btab pas in 004; it is printed clearly. dmar nag tu 'bar ba, 'blazing as dark red'; the other recension has dbus dmar nag alone. The print runs gcig and pa together across the line join and the ornament of the leaf front, and bgrad and pa at the next line join; both are divided here.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ གཡས་ ཀྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ པདྨ༔ བར་པ་ ན་ ཁ་ཊྭཾ་ག༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ དབྱུག་ཏོ༔ གཡོན་ གྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ དྲིལ་བུ༔ བར་བ་ ན་ བྷན་དྷ་ དམར་ གྱིས་ བཀང་བ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ རྔེ་ ཆུང་ བསྣམས་པ༔
sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in lotus; middle in khaṭvāṅga; last in staff; left's first in bell; middle in skull-cup red-with filled; last in drum(?) small holding;
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a lotus, the middle a khaṭvāṅga, the last a staff; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a skull-cup filled with red, the last a small drum(?);
sentences.n: padma, 'lotus'. kha TwaM ga, the khaṭvāṅga, here written in three syllables. dbyug to, 'staff, stick' (as dbyug pa). bhan dha dmar gyis bkang ba, 'a skull-cup filled with red', blood: bkang, the past stem of 'gengs, 'to fill'. rnge[?] chung is doubtful: the reader sees one stack with an e-vowel and no 'u after it, where the other recension has rnge'u chung; rnge is not a word known to the drafter. chung is 'small', and the thing is taken, as a guess, for a small drum (rnga, 'drum'); the sense is not sure. The print has bar pa on the right and bar ba on the left.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ པདྨ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ ཡབ་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་ མགུལ་ ནས་ འཁྱུད་ ཅིང༔ གཡོན་པས་ དུང་ དམར་ ཞལ་དུ་ སྟོབ་པ༔
sentences.l: The mother Padmakrodhīśvarī father's body to embracing; right-by neck at embracing and; left-by conch red mouth-to feeding;
sentences.i: his consort Padmakrodhīśvarī embraces the father's body: with her right hand she holds him round the neck, and with her left she puts a red conch to his mouth;
sentences.n: Padmakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the lotus family'; the other recension has sku la alone, without yab kyi. The print runs 'khril and ba together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ཞལ་སྦྱོར་ མངོན་སུམ་དུ་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནུབ་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ འོང་བས༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ དགའ་བ་ བསྒོམ་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Father-mother face-joining manifest-ly, own's brain's west from emerged, then, come-because: him at not fear! Not be-afraid! Him at not be-terrified! Joy meditate!
sentences.i: Father and mother in union come out of the west of your own brain, plainly before you. Do not fear him. Do not be afraid. Do not be terrified of him. Meditate on joy.
sentences.n: zhal sbyor, 'joining of faces', union: sbyor, 'to join', is the present stem of the verb whose past is the sbyar of zhal sbyar in 004; the other recension has zhal sbyor ba. mngon sum du, 'manifestly, before one's eyes'. nub nas, 'from the west', the quarter of the lotus family; the other recension has klad pa'i nang gi nub nas thon rang la 'char du 'ong pas, 'emerge from the west within the brain and dawn to you'. de la ma dngangs shig repeats de la, 'at him'. dga' ba bsgom shig, 'meditate on joy!': dga' ba, 'joy'; bsgom, the future stem of sgom, 'to meditate' (sgom / bsgoms / bsgom / sgoms), taking shig for the command. The other recension has dran pa bskyed cig, 'rouse mindfulness', here. The print runs pa'i and nub together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ སྐུར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ རང་ གི་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Own's knowing's body-as face-knowing do! Own's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid!
sentences.i: Recognise him as the form of your own awareness. He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid.
sentences.n: rang gi yi dam, 'your own yidam', where the other days have khyod rang gi, 'you yourself's'; the other recension has khyod rang gi here too and adds a second ma sngangs shig.

sentences.w: དོན་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དངོས་ ཡིན་པས་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ དང་ གྲོལ་བ་ དུས་མཉམ་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Amitābha father-mother itself is-because, devotion do! Face-knowing and freeing time-same-at comes.
sentences.i: In truth he is the Blessed One Amitābha himself with his consort, so have devotion. Recognising and freedom come at one and the same time.
sentences.n: Padma Heruka is Amitābha (Snang ba mtha' yas, 'Boundless Light'), the buddha of the fourth day (005). The print runs mos and pa together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ བསྒྲགས་པས་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam's deity being-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam deity, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: yi dam gyi lha yin par ngo shes, 'recognises that he is the yidam deity', as in 009, where the days before had yi dam du, 'as the yidam'. ngo is doubtful ([?]): no naro is seen over the nga, though the e-stroke of the next syllable runs over it and may hide it; ngo shes, 'recognise', is the only sense, and the line above has a clear ngo shes. The print runs nas and sangs together across the line join, here divided. The next part begins on the same line, with the twelfth day: yang de ltar ngo sprad kyang.
